results.step: collector ingest + query-back (step 1-2 of the discriminating test)
results.output: otelcol-contrib validate exited 0 after fixing exporter names (prometheusremotewrite, otlphttp/loki -- no native 'loki' exporter exists in this contrib build; its list of valid exporter type ids does not include 'loki'). First log push attempt failed: Loki returned HTTP 400 'includes structured metadata, but this feature is disallowed' until allow_structured_metadata: true was set. After that fix: emit_otlp.py returned {"metrics":{"status":200},"logs":{"status":200},"traces":{"status":200}} with empty partialSuccess (no ingest errors). Prometheus query for trading_order_fill_latency_ms returned 1 vector result with receipt_id=ord-000123, value 42.5. The counter ecosystem_codex_turn_token_usage_sum was exported as ecosystem_codex_turn_token_usage_sum_total=40518 (OTel cumulative-sum-to-counter renaming). Loki query_range for {service_name="us-equities-trading-runtime"} returned 2 streams (order_filled, risk_check) with the original receipt_id and event attributes intact. Traces were only sent to the debug exporter (no trace backend was in the pinned/candidate set); the debug log confirmed the ResourceSpans arrived with the correct span name and attributes, but no trace store was queried since none is a contested candidate here.

kill -9 issued to the otelcol, prometheus and loki PIDs simultaneously; ps -p on all three PIDs returned no output afterward (confirmed dead). Relaunching prometheus and loki against the *same* data directories and re-querying *before* emitting anything new returned the pre-kill data unchanged: 1 Prometheus series, 2 Loki streams. Restarting otelcol-contrib against the same config and emitting a second payload (tag=after_restart, receipt_id=ord-000456) succeeded (200/200/200) and both backends then showed 2 Prometheus series and 4 Loki streams (old + new), i.e. nothing was lost across the forced kill and no already-ingested data disappeared. What could still be lost is unmeasured here: any request in flight to the collector at the instant of kill -9 (none was in flight in this run), and Prometheus/Loki's own WAL segment not yet fsynced is a general property of both stores not specifically exercised by this test.

results.step: restic backup / check / restore / query parity (step 4)

This restic run covered only the Prometheus TSDB and Loki chunk/index directories created in this test; it did not cover a live broker/order-journal SQLite database, which neither sealed lane's restic receipt covered either (both flagged live_databases: 0).

results.step: sandbox-runtime confinement of the collector (step 5, original round)
results.output: `srt -d -c '<otelcol-contrib ...>'` launched successfully; debug log showed 'Wrapped command with bwrap (network, filesystem, seccomp(unix-block) restrictions)' and the collector logged 'Everything is ready' with its OTLP gRPC/HTTP receivers bound to 127.0.0.1:24317/24318 *inside the sandbox*. Sending the same emit_otlp.py payload to that port from the host then failed: Python raised `TimeoutError` / `URLError: <urlopen error timed out>` after a 10s timeout, and `curl -sv http://127.0.0.1:24318/` also timed out and was killed. `ps aux` confirmed the actual bwrap command line includes `--unshare-net`, which places the child in a new network namespace; the sandbox's HTTP/SOCKS egress proxy sockets (a Unix socket bridged via socat) are for the *sandboxed process's own outbound* requests, not for exposing its listening ports back to the host. Net result: under sandbox-runtime's default settings, the collector's own OTLP receiver becomes unreachable from outside the sandbox, so it cannot serve as the trading-runtime's ingest point while sandboxed this way. CORRECTED (fix round): this test wrapped the collector, a role the Codex lane never selected sandbox-runtime for (it selected srt to confine research workers' broker execution authority, not the always-on collector); see the fix-round c3 result below for the test of its actually-selected role. This step's raw result stands as evidence about wrapping a listening service, but the interpretation that it is a 'regression' for c3 has been withdrawn.

results.step: sandbox-runtime egress denial for a sandboxed worker (step 5, fix round -- tests c3's actually-selected role)
results.output: Re-run from the owned worktree (<owned-worktree>) as cwd, correcting the original round's cwd (which was the coordinator's main checkout, <coordinator-checkout>; confirmed via the deny-path enumeration lines in the debug log, no writes occurred but the wrong directory was in scope for path checks). Default settings, empty allowedHosts: `srt -d -c 'sleep 1; curl ... https://example.com'` produced `[SandboxDebug] No matching config rule, denying: example.com:443`, `[SandboxDebug] Connection blocked to example.com:443`, `curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`, exit 56. (A first attempt without the `sleep 1` raced the sandbox's internal port-3128 proxy listener and produced a misleading 'Couldn't connect to server' before the proxy had bound; retained as evidence of a startup race, not a security result.) With an explicit settings file (`network.allowedDomains: ["example.com"]`, `filesystem.allowWrite: ["."]`), the same command to https://example.com returned `[SandboxDebug] Allowed by config rule: example.com:443`, HTTP 200, exit 0; the same settings file with a request to https://api.github.com (not allow-listed) returned `[SandboxDebug] No matching config rule, denying: api.github.com:443`, exit 56. This directly demonstrates sandbox-runtime's actual selected role for this row's requirement -- denying a sandboxed worker's own outbound network access by default while remaining controllable via an explicit allowlist -- working as designed. Raw logs committed alongside this receipt: evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260923/obs-compare/logs-fixround/{egress-default-firstattempt-raced.log,egress-default-retry.log,egress-allowlisted.log,egress-allowlisted-otherhost-denied.log}; full scratch retained at <host-cache-path>/sota-refresh-20260923/obs-compare/fixround/.

results.step: restic hot backup under concurrent writes (step 4, fix round -- corrects the original round's cold-backup-only scope)
results.output: Fresh Prometheus (29490/29590) and Loki (23400/23500) instances and an otelcol-contrib collector (24417/24418) were started in a new scratch area and left running (not stopped) for this test. A 40-iteration emitter loop (0.3s interval, ~12s total) was started in the background; `pgrep`/process listing confirmed the loop's bash and python child processes were both alive when `restic backup <prometheus_dir> <loki_dir> --tag obs-compare-hot` was issued mid-loop. Backup completed in the same second it started ('processed 7 files, 37.559 KiB in 0:00', snapshot 911db955) while the loop was still actively posting. `restic check --read-data` afterward reported 'no errors were found' (100% of 1 snapshot, 2 packs read) -- no corruption from the concurrent-write backup. `restic restore latest --target <empty_dir> --verify` reported 'Restored 31 files/dirs (37.559 KiB)' and 'finished verifying 7 files' with no failures. Fresh Prometheus/Loki instances (29590/23500) launched against the restored directories served the same queries used throughout this receipt and returned 27 Prometheus series and 54 Loki streams, versus 41 series and 82 streams on the still-running live instances queried after the full 40-iteration loop completed. The lower restored counts are expected and correct: the hot backup captured a consistent point-in-time snapshot from partway through the write loop, not the final state, and none of the restored data was corrupted or missing relative to what had been durably written by the moment restic ran. This satisfies a live/hot backup test that was absent from the original round (which stopped both backends with SIGTERM before backing them up).

per_component_verdicts.name: restic
per_component_verdicts.summary: CORRECTED (fix round, independent review finding): the original-round restic test stopped both backends with SIGTERM before backing them up -- a cold backup of stopped stores, not a live one, despite the original summary claiming it closed the 'live_databases 0' limitation. That claim has been withdrawn for the original test. A genuine fix-round hot-backup test now covers the gap directly: restic backup was run against Prometheus and Loki data directories while both processes stayed running and a background emitter loop was actively posting new data, confirmed alive via process listing at backup time. `restic check --read-data` found no errors and `restore --verify` succeeded with no verification failures; fresh instances against the restored (mid-loop) snapshot served correct, uncorrupted, if necessarily partial, query results (27/54 vs the live 41/82 series/streams after the loop finished) -- exactly the expected behavior of a consistent point-in-time snapshot taken during concurrent writes, not evidence of loss or corruption. Restic is therefore demonstrated to work for both a cold backup (original round) and a hot/concurrent-write backup (fix round) of these two observability backends specifically. It remains untested here for a live broker/order-journal database, off-host destination, key escrow, or a longer/heavier concurrent-write window, so it does not close every restic limitation on record -- but for the observability backends specifically, restic is now demonstrated to work under both conditions, which the Claude lane's set (lacking restic) cannot claim for recovery at all.

per_component_verdicts.name: sandbox-runtime
per_component_verdicts.summary: CORRECTED (fix round, independent review finding): the original round judged c3 against a role no lane actually selected it for -- wrapping the always-on collector as a listening service -- and called the resulting inbound-unreachable result a 'regression'. The Codex lane selected sandbox-runtime to confine research workers and deny broker execution authority (why_selected: 'sandbox-runtime filesystem restrictions'; open_gaps: 'Sandbox network denial was configured but not exercised'), not to wrap the collector. The row's own requirement text -- 'retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority' -- makes egress/authority confinement of a worker part of what this row is judging, so 'needed: unclear' was also wrong; a form of it is needed. The original inbound-unreachable observation is not a regression: it directly confirms srt's --unshare-net network-namespace isolation is real and functioning as designed (the installed srt source at linux-sandbox-utils.js always adds --unshare-net on Linux when network restriction is active). The fix round ran the actually-discriminating test for c3's selected role: a sandboxed worker's OUTBOUND (egress) request. Default settings denied it (curl exit 56, 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', 'No matching config rule, denying: example.com:443'); an explicit allowedHosts entry let the same host through while a non-listed host stayed denied under the same settings file. This is native_proven evidence that sandbox-runtime does deny a worker's default egress and does so controllably, which is what the row's broker-authority-denial language calls for. It is marked not_comparable rather than qualified because it was never tested end-to-end wrapping an actual research-worker process attempting a broker call (only a generic curl proxy for 'egress to an arbitrary host'), and because it plays a different structural role in the layer than the always-on collector/backends (worker confinement vs. an ingest/storage pipeline component), so it is not a like-for-like substitute for or against opentelemetry-collector-contrib/Prometheus/Loki in the contested three-item sets. Whether wrapping the collector itself is ever needed remains answered 'no' by the original test, which stands on its own (mislabeled interpretation only, not a mislabeled result).

All four version-pinned components (opentelemetry-collector-contrib, loki, prometheus, restic) already matched the newest upstream release at run time, so this is an executed same-version comparison of the contested candidate set, not a version-upgrade qualification. sandbox-runtime's upstream latest release was not separately resolved via gh api in this run.

Traces were sent only to the debug exporter; no trace backend is in either contested set, so trace storage/query-back was not exercised beyond confirming the collector accepts and logs OTLP trace data.

The kill -9 test used one simultaneous kill of all three processes with no in-flight request at the moment of the kill; a request that is mid-flight during a real crash, or an unflushed WAL segment older than the last successful checkpoint, is not covered.

Restic backup/restore covered only the Prometheus TSDB and Loki chunk/index directories created fresh in this test session (both a cold backup of stopped processes in the original round, and a genuine hot backup under a ~12s/40-iteration concurrent-write window in the fix round); it did not cover a live broker/order-journal database, an off-host repository destination, independent key escrow, or a longer/heavier concurrent-write window. The same live-database gap both sealed lanes already flagged for restic remains open for anything beyond these two observability backends' data directories.

The sandbox-runtime egress-denial re-test (fix round) used a generic `curl` process as the 'sandboxed worker', not an actual research-worker process attempting a broker call; it demonstrates srt's default-deny/allowlist-controllable egress behavior in general, not confinement of the specific worker binaries this layer would run. Only two settings-file configurations were tried (empty allowedHosts; allowedHosts=["example.com"]); the full settings-file schema (e.g. shared-network-namespace or per-process options) was not read end to end. Whether wrapping the always-on collector itself is ever useful remains 'no' per the original round's own result, which is unchanged; only the interpretation of that result for c3's needed/verdict fields was corrected.

This comparison did not touch or modify the live production observability stack running on this host: `ps -p 370,381,386` at the start and end of the fix round both show loki (370), otelcol (381) and prometheus (386) running continuously since 2026-09-22T11:04:18 on the ecosystem's regular ports (19090/13100), confirming the original round's ambiguous 'pid 386/386-successor' phrasing did not reflect an actual restart -- it was inaccurate wording, now corrected. All test instances (original and fix round) used distinct loopback ports (24317/24318, 29090/29190, 23100/23200, 29490/29590, 23400/23500, 24417/24418) and scratch data directories under <host-cache-path>/sota-refresh-20260923/obs-compare/ and its fixround/ subdirectory.

The scratch directory (<host-cache-path>/sota-refresh-20260923/obs-compare/, including a fixround/ subdirectory with the egress and hot-backup test artifacts) was NOT deleted after this run, correcting the original round's 'fully cleaned up' claim, which was true only of running processes and bound ports, not of files on disk. It is retained as this receipt's raw-output recovery path: config/*.yml, logs/*.log, emit_otlp.py, restic-repo/ (including its key material -- a local-only test repository with a hardcoded test password, not a secret worth protecting, but noted for completeness), restic-restore/, and fixround/{config,logs,restic-repo-hot,restic-restore-hot,emit_otlp_hot.py,fixround-preregistration.md,egress-*.log}.
